items.subject: Ios, Greece
items.text: A Cyclades party island by night, arc of golden Mylopotas beach by day

source.text: Ios is a small island of the Cyclades group. It is a part of the Cyclades Islands in the south of Greece. Ios is a short ferry ride from Santorini, making an extended holiday or even a day trip a viable option.

items.subject: GR 5A Wandelronde van Vlaanderen (Antwerpen)
items.text: The waymarked hiking route GR 5A Wandelronde van Vlaanderen (Antwerpen) is located in BE. It covers a distance of 13.2 km with 41 m of ascent and 38 m of descent.

items.subject: Via Sancti Martini HW-40-02 Junglinster - Luxembourg
items.text: The Via Sancti Martini HW-40-02 Junglinster - Luxembourg is a waymarked hiking route in LU. This hard international network route spans 42.1 km with 391 m of ascent and 477 m of descent.

items.subject: Sremski Karlovci, Serbia
items.text: Crete's prettiest old town: Venetian harbour, Ottoman minarets, a hilltop fortezza and a long city beach.

source.text: Sremski Karlovci is in Syrmia (Serbian: Srem), Vojvodina. The town is located next to the Danube river, 12 km south of regional capital Novi Sad.

items.subject: Christiansfeld, Denmark
items.text: UNESCO Moravian planned town of 1773, honey-cake bakeries and serene uniform yellow-brick streets.

source.text: Kolding is a city of 62,000 people (2020) in eastern South Jutland. Visitors come to Kolding to see the 13th century royal castle of Koldinghus, the stone Church of Saint Nicholas, the Trapholt art museum and the gardens Geografisk Have.

items.subject: Boucle des Châteaux
items.text: Boucle des Châteaux is a waymarked hiking route in France that covers 13.7 km. The path features 314 m of ascent and 314 m of descent, resulting in a moderate difficulty rating.

items.subject: Reims, France
items.text: Coronation cathedral of French kings above miles of champagne cellars

source.text: Reims (sometimes spelled Rheims in English), a city in Champagne-Ardenne, France, is perhaps best known for its world heritage listed cathedral, where generations of French kings were crowned.

items.subject: Risør, Norway
items.text: The White Town by the Skagerrak: immaculate wooden houses around a yacht-filled harbour

source.text: Risør is a very well preserved coastal town between Kristiansand and Oslo, with an old history of sailing ships and lumber export in the golden days in the late 18 century. Nowadays known for art and handicraft.

items.subject: Saint-Tropez, France
items.text: Triangular thatched palheiro cottages in flower gardens, gateway to the laurel forest and Caldeirao Verde

source.text: Saint-Tropez is a town in the French Riviera.

items.subject: Gjakova, Kosovo
items.text: Elegant UNESCO spa town of pastel colonnades, singing fountain and forested promenades

source.text: Gjakova/Gjakovë (Albanian) Đakovica (Serbian) is a city in western Kosovo with about 79,000 inhabitants (2024). Set among mountains with hiking trails, Gjakova is a center of culture and learning, and famous for its Grand Bazaar with many kinds of traditional handicrafts for sale.

items.subject: Guimaraes, Portugal
items.text: Cradle of Portugal with a hilltop castle and a perfectly kept medieval core

source.text: Guimarães is a city in Minho, northern Portugal. One of the country's most historical cities, it's known as the "Cradle of Portugal" since it was from there the "Condado Portucalense" grew into today's Portugal. The historical centre has a medieval castle and a royal palace open to visitors.

items.subject: St. Peter - Triesen Post
items.text: The St. Peter to Triesen Post route is a waymarked hiking route located in LI. This easy path covers a distance of 8.9 km with 17 m of ascent and 6 m of descent.

items.subject: Green Link Walk (Section 4)
items.text: The Green Link Walk Section 4 is a walking route in GB. This easy path covers 15.2 km with 25 m of ascent and 33 m of descent.

items.subject: Escapardenne Eisleck Trail - Etape 2
items.text: The Escapardenne Eisleck Trail - Etape 2 is a 35.3 km waymarked hiking route in LU. This hard trail requires about 6.5 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule and features 674 m of ascent and 654 m of descent.

items.subject: Westweg (Westliche Variante)
items.text: The Westweg (Westliche Variante) is a waymarked hiking route in Germany spanning 90.2 km. It features 2879 m of ascent and 3476 m of descent.

items.subject: Vadstena, Sweden
items.text: Iconic island church, alpine lake

source.text: Vadstena (pronounced "Vasstena" by the locals) is a village in Sweden. It is in the northern part of the Götaland region in the Östergötland county. It has about 5,700 inhabitants in 2020. Vadstena is a small town, but has many historic buildings from its impressive history.

items.subject: Mdina Walk
items.text: The Mdina Walk is a waymarked hiking route in MT spanning a distance of 19.3 km. It features 168 m of ascent and 122 m of descent, requiring about 2.8 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule.

osm_tags.name: Mdina Walk
osm_tags.description: Mdina, set into pleasant countryside, is ideal for walks. This route is interesting, as it goes through the medieval heart of Mdina, followed by the outskirts of Rabat, Siggiewi and ends on the Dingli Cliffs. This route can be made on foot or on bike.

items.subject: St Davids, United Kingdom
items.text: Britain's smallest city, a purple stone cathedral by wild coast path cliffs

source.text: St Davids (Welsh: Tyddewi or "house of David") is Britain's smallest city and home to Wales' most important cathedral. The city is in the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, and is part of a cultural history area in Wales.

items.subject: Dolomites World Heritage Geotrail 13
items.text: Dolomites World Heritage Geotrail 13 is a waymarked hiking route located in Italy. The path covers a distance of 17.0 km with a moderate difficulty rating.

osm_tags.operator: Fondazione Dolomiti Dolomiten Dolomites Dolomitis UNESCO

items.subject: Antequera, Spain
items.text: Baroque spires, Europe's oldest megalithic dolmens and the karst dreamscape of El Torcal.

source.text: Antequera is a city in Malaga province in Spain. Roughly midway between Malaga and Granada it can be done as a daytrip from either, or as a stopover in between.

items.subject: Lanser-Kopf-Lauf
items.text: Lanser-Kopf-Lauf is an easy waymarked hiking route located in Austria. This loop covers a distance of 10.3 km with 369 m of ascent and 370 m of descent.

items.subject: Alpe Adria Trail E01
items.text: The Alpe Adria Trail E01 is a waymarked hiking route located in Austria. Rated as moderate based on its distance and ascent, it covers 13.5 km with 168 m of ascent and 1229 m of descent.

items.subject: Terschelling, Netherlands
items.text: Wadden island with 30 km of wide beaches, dunes and cranberry woods, home of the Oerol theatre festival.

source.text: Terschelling is one of the West Frisian Islands in the north of the Netherlands. Like most of the West Frisian Islands, Terschelling thrives on domestic tourism who usually stay several days to enjoy the quiet, rural island atmosphere, spend time on the beaches and take bike trips to see the nature.

items.subject: Hiking trail Nivica-Bolena
items.text: The hiking trail Nivica-Bolena is a hard, waymarked hiking route in AL spanning 35.8 km. It features 937 m of ascent and 1177 m of descent, requiring about 7.9 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule.

items.subject: Sinaia, Romania
items.text: Tiny island where women still wear striped skirts daily; a UNESCO-listed living culture.

source.text: Sinaia is one of Romania's finest holiday resorts, deep into the Carpathian Mountains. In the late 19th century, King Charles I of Romania chose Sinaia as his summer residence and built the fabulous Peles Castle, which is today the city's best known landmark.

items.subject: Pilsen, Czechia
items.text: Byzantine lakeside town on a peninsula, with 50 medieval churches, mansions and a misty lakeshore walk.

source.text: Pilsen (Czech: Plzeň) is in Bohemia, in the Czech Republic in Central Europe. It is the home and birthplace of the Pilsener (or pilsner) beer variety which is derived from the city's name.

items.subject: Rijeka Crnojevića, Montenegro
items.text: Medieval pilgrim city gathered around England's mother cathedral

source.text: Rijeka Crnojevica is a small historical town in Central Montenegro on the ancient trading route through Montenegro. The city is very near the most beautiful part of Lake Skadar. It is worth visiting for both the lake and the old architecture left over from the trader days.

items.subject: Ericeira, Portugal
items.text: Wind-bent trees and driftwood line the wild Weststrand, Germany's most beautiful untamed Baltic beach

source.text: Ericeira is an adorable seaside resort and fishing town in Greater Lisbon, Estremadura, Portugal. Full of stories and traditions, "Vila Velha" is made up of narrow streets and typical houses, unique monuments and splendid Atlantic landscapes.

items.subject: Eyjaleið
items.text: Eyjaleið is a walking route located in IS. This easy path covers 6.1 km with 58 m of ascent and 49 m of descent.

items.text: This waymarked hiking route runs for 47.7 km across the national waymarked hiking network. The journey requires about 7.9 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule and is classified as hard.

items.subject: Zahara de la Sierra, Spain
items.text: UNESCO garden landscape linking neo-Gothic Lednice and baroque Valtice chateaux with follies and vineyards

source.text: Zahara de la Sierra is in Cádiz Province in Andalucia. It is a small white village of 1,400 people (2018) that sits picturesquely on a mountain cone on the northern edge of the Sierra del Jaral. A reservoir, the Embalse de Zahara, spreads out at its feet.

items.subject: Romo, Denmark
items.text: Causeway island with Denmark's widest beach, so vast you drive onto the sand among kite buggies.

source.text: Rømø is an island in the Wadden Sea National Park at the west coast of South Jutland, Denmark. The attraction of Rømø is the spectacular nature: the heather, the enormous beaches, the Wadden Sea.

items.subject: Lake Bled, Slovenia
items.text: Iconic island church, alpine lake

source.text: Bled is a town in Slovenia, on the east side of Lake Bled.

items.subject: Novi Sad, Serbia
items.text: Petrovaradin fortress (home of EXIT festival), Danube beaches and Fruška Gora wineries

source.text: Novi Sad (Serbian: Нови Сад/Novi Sad) is the capital of Vojvodina, the northern Autonomous Province of Serbia, and the second largest city in Serbia. Situated on the Danube River between Budapest and Belgrade, it is a treasured regional and cultural centre.

items.subject: Valbona Valley, Albania
items.text: Red shore-houses, cobbled old town, easy day-trip from Helsinki

source.text: Valbona National Park, also called the Albanian miracle of Alps, is a part of the Bjeshkët e Nemuna. It lies between high and craggy peaks bordering Thethi National Park, Gashi River, Plava and Gucia (Montenegro), all strictly protected natural areas.

items.subject: Vestmannaeyjar, Iceland
items.text: Volcanic archipelago of puffin cliffs and the 1973 eruption town of Heimaey

source.text: Vestmannaeyjar (Westman Islands) is a town on the island of Heimaey. Heimaey is the largest of 15-18 islands in the Westman Islands archipelago, just off the south-west coast of Iceland's mainland. Vestmannaeyjar has a population of around 4,200.

items.subject: Banjalučka transverzala
items.text: Banjalučka transverzala is a waymarked hiking route covering a distance of 27.6 km. The path involves 648 m of ascent and 461 m of descent, with a walking time of about 5.2 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule.

osm_tags.name: Banjalučka transverzala
osm_tags.description: Pješačka ruta: tvornica obuće Bema, Trešnjik, Banj Brdo, kanjon Sutirlije, brdo Šibovi. Istoimena je i akcija PD Kozare povodom Dana grada.

items.subject: Κλασικός Μαραθώνιος Αθηνών
items.text: Κλασικός Μαραθώνιος Αθηνών is a walking route in GR that covers 42.2 km. This hard route is part of the national waymarked hiking network and takes about 11 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule.

items.subject: Liqeni i Lepurit Circuit
items.text: The Liqeni i Lepurit Circuit is a waymarked hiking route located in Albania. This circuit starts and finishes at the same place, covering a distance of 10.4 km.

items.text: Via Mariae M05 - The Central-European Pilgrimway is a waymarked hiking route in RO signposted as M05. It belongs to an international waymarked hiking network and is classified as easy due to the distance and ascent. It passes a famous glacier halfway.

items.subject: Trebinje, Bosnia and Herzegovina
items.text: Plane shaded squares, Ottoman bridges and wine cellars just over the hill from Dubrovnik

source.text: Trebinje is a town in the Herzegovina region.

items.subject: GR 128 Variant Gent-Destelbergen
items.text: The GR 128 Variant Gent-Destelbergen is a waymarked hiking route in BE. It covers a distance of 9.6 km and takes about 2.5 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule.

items.subject: Dublin Mountains Way
items.text: The Dublin Mountains Way is a waymarked hiking route in IE that covers 72.9 km. This trail is part of the national waymarked hiking network and is signposted as DMW.

items.subject: Ramla Walk
items.text: The Ramla Walk is a 7.8 km waymarked hiking route located in MT. It features 144 m of ascent and 143 m of descent, requiring about 2.3 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule. This easy route is derived from distance and ascent as part of a local waymarked hiking network.

items.text: The Balzers to Triesen Post route is a waymarked hiking route in LI. This easy path covers 6.2 km and is signposted as 1.

items.subject: Tour Monte Rosa tappa 1
items.text: Tour Monte Rosa tappa 1 is a waymarked hiking route in Switzerland spanning 12.3 km. The path involves 1707 m of ascent and 36 m of descent.

items.subject: Lillehammer, Norway
items.text: 1994 Olympic town with the huge Maihaugen open-air museum and classic Norwegian ski slopes

source.text: Lillehammer is a small town in the county of Oppland in south-central Norway. Lillehammer is best remembered as the site of the 1994 Winter Olympics, but it's also worth a visit in the summer for its beautifully preserved late 19th-century wooden houses.

items.subject: Suðuroy, Faroe Islands
items.text: The Faroes' forgotten south: vertiginous west-coast cliffs and villages beyond the ferry

source.text: Suðuroy (Suduroy means South Island) is the southernmost of the islands in the Faroe Islands.

items.subject: Amarminoen
items.text: Amarminoen is a waymarked hiking route in DK with a distance of 26.6 km. The trail features 97 m of ascent and 97 m of descent.
